findings.title: SQL feature gate is inverted and always returns false
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions sets enabled to the negation of FlagSqlExpressions and then returns false from both branches, so the flag is never actually honored and the function cannot enable SQL under any configuration. Today that fails closed, which is what this CVE fix wants, but the inverted condition is a landmine: changing the final return to true (the obvious cleanup of a function named enable) would turn SQL expressions back on exactly when the feature flag is disabled, reopening the DuckDB path this PR is meant to kill.

findings.title: DuckDB SQL injection sink left intact; only one entry point is gated
findings.body: TablesList still interpolates the caller-supplied SQL into SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s') after only doubling single quotes, which is the same string-built DuckDB command that CVE-2024-9264 abused for RCE/LFI. The new enableSqlExpressions check lives only in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery. UnmarshalSQLCommand in pkg/expr/sql_command.go still calls NewSQLCommand, which calls TablesList and, on success, Execute still calls QueryFramesInto. Those methods are stubbed to return "not implemented" in pkg/expr/sql/db.go, so the exploit does not run today, but the injection primitive and the second entry point remain. Restoring a real RunCommands/QueryFramesInto (or a partial stub that returns nil error) executes attacker-controlled SQL again with no feature-flag gate on that path.
